questions.q: Which SageMaker resource keeps billing until you explicitly delete it?
options: A registered model version in the registry
questions.explain: Real-time endpoints keep instances running around the clock until deleted. Training and batch jobs stop billing when they finish.

questions.q: A nightly campaign list is scored once a day and nobody needs instant answers. Which inference option fits best?
options: A real-time endpoint with a very large instance
questions.explain: Batch transform is for offline scoring of a large dataset with no persistent endpoint; you pay for the instance only while the job runs.

questions.q: Why did the lesson describe its $0.20 per instance-hour rate as hypothetical?
options: It is the exact price of the smallest instance
AWS does not charge for endpoints
It was chosen so the ratios between scenarios are easy to see; real prices depend on instance type and region
It includes the Savings Plans discount
questions.explain: The rate is a placeholder. Always look up current pricing for your instance type and region.

questions.q: Managed spot training can reduce training cost per the AWS docs. What must you accept in exchange?
options: Spot instances can be interrupted, so use checkpointing unless the job is short
Training must run in the notebook itself
questions.explain: Spot capacity can be interrupted, which can lengthen jobs. The docs recommend checkpointing unless the job completes quickly.

questions.q: In the lesson's cleanup checklist, which set of calls removes the serving resources?
options: delete_endpoint, delete_endpoint_config and delete_model, plus delete_monitoring_schedule if one exists
questions.explain: The serving stack is the endpoint, its configuration, the model, and any monitoring schedule. Deleting only the model leaves the endpoint billing.
